summary.intent: Manage a multi-night, multi-wave parallel PR development effort on CipherBox v2: kick off decomposed GitHub issues via worktree-isolated agents, drive the CodeRabbit/macroscope review queue while the user was AFK/merging, resolve blocked design decisions for rotation seams (#1025/#1026) via ADRs, and finally sweep stale issue-number references out of code comments (#1031) with a regrowth guard.
summary.outcome: Six+ PRs merged overnight closing dozens of issues; branch protection restored on main; ADRs 0003/0004 drafted and merged in cipher-box-next resolving #1025/#1026 design blockers with blueprint/CONTEXT.md updated accordingly; #1031 completed — ~420+ stale issue refs stripped from ~120 files, a `check-tracker-refs.mjs` CI guard added to prevent regrowth, all tests/lint/wasm32 green, changes committed.

repo: wasm32 is a 32-bit target: usize is 4 bytes not 8, causing copy_from_slice length-mismatch panics invisible to cargo check/build for wasm32 — only running tests (wasm32-wasip1) catches it.
`cargo check --workspace` never builds wasm32; must explicitly `cargo check -p cipherbox-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` to catch cross-crate breaks.

CodeRabbit is incremental and dedupes by head SHA — flipping a PR ready a second time on an unchanged SHA answers 'Already reviewed', not a fresh review; `@coderabbitai full review` is the override but is itself subject to fair-usage rate limiting.

CodeRabbit has two verdict surfaces: findings land in a submitted review body (pulls/N/reviews), but a CLEAN verdict produces no review event at all — only an in-place edit of the status comment. A poller must watch both, and the bot's GitHub login is `coderabbitai[bot]`, not `coderabbitai`.

The status comment is a single mutable surface — repeated `@coderabbitai review` requests overwrite it in place, destroying prior evidence (e.g. a clean verdict) if you retry after already getting an answer.

macroscope (third PR reviewer) initially reviewed draft PRs; user later configured it to only review 'ready' PRs, matching CodeRabbit/Greptile — meaning draft PRs now get zero review coverage from any tool.

ADR mechanism lives in FSM1/cipher-box-next's `decisions/` directory, not `docs/adr/` in cipher-box (that's dead v1 residue whose ADR 0003 specifies a retired AES-256-GCM primitive). ADRs are written only when a decision amends/extends a frozen wayfinder decision or fills a genuine corpus gap; landed via a PR to cipher-box-next, then `Status:` flipped to 'implemented in cipher-box#N (merged)' via follow-up commit.

GitHub Actions variable scoping: repo-scope vars are visible everywhere; environment-scoped vars (e.g. `staging`) are only visible to jobs declaring `environment: staging` — a workflow with no `environment:` key sees only repo-scope.

Branch protection required-status-checks must target the `if: always()` Result gate names (e.g. 'Desktop Build Result', 'Contract Suite Result'), not individual matrix-leg job names, or path-filtered/skipped matrix legs deadlock the merge.
AGENTS.md rule 8: decode-side fail-closed rejects require a release-active encode-side Err, never debug_assert! — repeatedly the source of real bugs found by review gates this session.

The repo previously had ~420+ stale `#NNNN` issue references scattered across code comments (86-91% pointing at already-closed issues); two-digit `#NN Dn` wayfinder-decision citations (e.g. `#26 D2`, `#38 D6`) are a distinct, intentional pattern citing the frozen cipher-box-next decision corpus and should be kept, not stripped.

Semantic merge conflicts (both PRs individually MERGEABLE, combination fails to compile) are real and recurring in this repo — verifying requires actually building a scratch worktree with all branches merged, not just checking pairwise `git merge-tree`.

code.finding: Epoch-lag predicate was applied to scope roots, which structurally can never lag their own floor (rotate/cascade publish-then-raise-floor) — the sweep should target interior nodes per the corrected ADR 0003.

ChildRef.ipns_name lives in the read body — proves a write-plane name wave must rewrite every parent's child refs (ADR 0004), since read-only grantees can't derive interior names from write_scope_seed.
open_grant_blob returns write_scope_seed: None for read-only grants — confirms read-only survivors are stranded after a write-plane name wave unless the read body is rewritten.

Precedent pattern for WriteWavePublisher: 'the read body and envelope fields a republish preserves come from the node's own current record, gated — the rotation carries neither.' Used to justify #1026 D1 (publisher re-resolves via current_name).

New CI guard added, wired as 'Tracker Refs' job + `pnpm lint:tracker-refs`, that fails on bare `#[0-9]{3,4}` in comments across crates/, apps/, packages/, landing/, tools/ while exempting repo-qualified refs (e.g. `FSM1/cipher-box-next#32`).

Engine::start touched by multiple concurrent PRs on exactly one line each (e.g. Rc::new(SessionIdentity::derive) removal) roughly 30 lines above spawn_* calls threaded by a sibling PR — the pattern that let file-ownership-scoped agents avoid semantic collisions.

workflow: Never apply a review-tool suggestion literally — it's a symptom report, not a spec. Twice this session a literal fix would have introduced a worse bug (a denial-of-revocation vector, and moving rather than removing an availability window); catch this by re-running the review gates on the fix itself.

When scheduling review-slot polling jobs, always compute deadlines from absolute epoch seconds, never string-compare HHMM — a naive `[ "2336" -ge "0131" ]` numeric-string comparison fires immediately and burns a review slot.
Space consecutive rate-limited review slots from the actual verdict timestamp of the prior review, not from 'now' — otherwise a slot can land inside the still-active rate-limit window.
`nohup ... &` background jobs are not harness-tracked and produce no completion notification — always use the tracked background-task mechanism for anything you need to be notified about.

Before merging a PR based on issue-body claims, verify the defect/premise against actual code — five separate times an issue body was wrong (wrong file, wrong premise, dead field referenced, unsound acceptance criterion, false 'already landed' claim), each caught only because an agent was briefed to verify before implementing.

For overnight/large parallel PR waves: assign disjoint file-ownership sets per agent, then verify pairwise AND combined-tree compiles/tests in an isolated worktree with no shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR before flipping any PR to ready — this repeatedly caught (and ruled out false-positive) semantic conflicts.
Stale local node_modules can produce false TS2307 typecheck/test failures that look like real breakage — always re-run pnpm install before trusting a red verification result.

friction: GitHub API connectivity flapped repeatedly overnight ('connection refused'), causing failed pushes, false ABORT results, and requiring retry-with-connectivity-check wrappers throughout.
Self-authored scheduling bug (HHMM string comparison) burned one CodeRabbit review slot and ~1 hour of overnight throughput.
Self-authored poller bug (stale review-body read without a timestamp fence) caused a false 're-review' report on #1058 that reused already-fixed findings.

Self-authored login-filter bug (`coderabbitai` vs `coderabbitai[bot]`) made the clean-verdict status-comment surface invisible all night, leading to two wrong diagnoses (SHA-dedup, then daily cap) for #1065 and destructive retries that overwrote the actual clean verdict evidence — required the user to correct via screenshot.

CodeRabbit's incremental-review dedup by head SHA meant a PR accidentally flipped-ready during the buggy scheduling window became permanently un-re-reviewable at that commit, needing an explicit 'full review' override subject to its own rate limit.
One agent (crates/core sweep) overstepped scope and stripped two-digit wayfinder decision refs that were meant to be kept, requiring a manual revert pass.
Stale `apps/web/node_modules` produced a false-red verification run (TS2307 errors) that had to be diagnosed before trusting it as a real regression.

One agent's `--no-verify` commit justification ('diff is Rust-only, hooks are no-ops') was factually wrong — a blueprint markdown file was in the diff with real markdownlint violations that no CI workflow would have caught (`lint:md` script exists but isn't wired to any workflow).
